To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of metformin, sulfonylurea, and glitazone drugs is associated with a reduction in the incidence of CV events in patients with T2DM, and that this effect may be independent of their effects on glycemic control.
intensive glucose lowering is not beneficial in reducing CV events in T2MD individuals and that a comprehensive approach to global CV risk factor management is beneficial in T2DM patients.

intensive glucose lowering with a sulfonylurea (glibenclamide) or insulin (insulin glargine), compared with standard glucose-lowering treatment, does not reduce macrovascular events or mortality in T2DM patients with a history of cardiovascular disease, and that the addition of a sulfonyl urea (glibe- clamide) or insulin glargine to metformin in patients with T2DM and no history of cardiovascular disease does not reduce cardiovascular events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of glucose lowering drugs to reduce cardiovascular (CV) events and mortality in individuals with diabetes mellitus.
the development of new methods of treatment for patients with T2DM.
the development and application of new methods for the treatment of type 2 diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the best approach to reducing the risk for CV disease in T2DM is to achieve and sustain near normal glucose levels in the context of an aggressive multifactorial strategy to reduce other CV risk factors.

the evidence supports the use of intensive glycemic control in T2DM patients to reduce microvascular events and that the evidence supports intensive blood pressure and lipid control to reduce CV events.

the use of any glucose-lowering drug, including metformin, thiazolidinediones, sulfonylureas, meglitinides, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitors, and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists, in combination with lifestyle modifications and other CV risk factor modifications, is beneficial in reducing CV events and mortality in T2DM patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the potential of glucose-lowering agents to reduce CV events is limited.
the potential for glucose-lowering drugs is to reduce CV events in patients with T2DM, although there is a need to further investigate this potential.
intensive glucose lowering in T2DM is not recommended for the purpose of reducing CV events.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current data do not support a specific glucose-lowering agent or class of agents as superior to others in reducing CV events in T2MD individuals.
the use of glucose-lowering agents in the setting of a comprehensive strategy of global CV risk factor management is associated with a reduction in CV events.
there is no single glucose-lowering agent that has been proven to reduce macrovascular events in TDM individuals.
